newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Binariang denies plans to sell phone unit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Binariang denies plans to sell phone unit.

text.p: Malaysian telecommunications firm Binariang Sdn Bhd on Tuesday denied it was selling its cellular service to a rival as reported by a local daily.
In a statement, the company said its Maxis Mobile service will remain a core business.

"We would like to categorically deny all speculation that we are holding talks with any party to sell our Maxis Mobile operation and we hope that this will set the record straight,' Binariang's executive director C.Y. Chin said in a statement.

The Sun newspaper said on Tuesday that Binariang and Cellular Communications Network (M) Sdn Bhd (Celcom) were believed to be holding talks on the posibility of Binariang selling its digital phone service.
Celcom is a wholly-owned subsidiary of telecommunications group Technology Resources Industries Bhd and operates an analogue and a digital cellular phone system.
Chin said Binariang's cellular service which currently has 150,000 customers "is very strongly supported by the public".
Binariang plans to double its communication base stations from the 300 set up last year.
Binariang is a joint venture between Malaysian shareholders led by tycoon T. Ananda Krishnan and U.S. West International, which has a 20 percent stake.
